source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text: Fruit thinning is described as necessary because a durian tree that sets an excessive fruit load will produce many undersized, poorly-filled fruit rather than fewer well-developed ones, and can also exhaust the tree's reserves in a way that reduces the following year's flowering. Thinning should remove the smallest, latest-set, misshapen, or crowded fruit within each cluster, leaving well-spaced fruit with room to reach full size, broadly matching the staged thinning approach described in Source A of this batch.
